instruction: Reformat the spreadsheet so all data fits on one PDF page, then export it.

metadata.explanation: Task requires adjusting layout to fit all spreadsheet data on one PDF page. Evaluator verifies the PDF has exactly 1 page with valid dimensions. Very similar to original task with paraphrased instruction.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the primary requirement: PDF exported with exactly 1 page
Getter logic is correct: reads PDF using pypdf, extracts page_count and dimensions from the expected file path
Metric logic is correct: verifies page_count == 1 and validates dimensions > 0 to ensure non-empty page
Metric correctly handles expected parameter - directly accesses expected.get('page_count') since framework returns rules dict directly when type='rule'
Data flow is semantically correct: getter extracts PDF state -> metric compares page count and dimensions -> returns binary score
Expected value (page_count: 1) is semantically correct for 'fit all data on a single PDF page'
State accessibility is good: PDF file persists after export, no postconfig needed
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding verification that spreadsheet content is actually rendered in the PDF (e.g., check for text extraction or minimum content size)
The current implementation would pass for an empty 1-page PDF, though dimension validation mitigates this risk
Could enhance robustness by checking PDF content contains expected data elements from the spreadsheet
